# Low-poly island — Style Prompt

> A tiny faceted world seen through an orthographic isometric lens: hexagonal tile columns floating in a teal sea, a pale sky with no horizon that swallows the far side of the island in haze, and everything that appears arrives with a bounce: tiles rise one per beat with a foam ring and spray, trees pop, houses drop and squash, a lighthouse lights up. Building is the performance; the camera cuts between a tight close-up on one arrival and the whole island growing, and ends on the finished world afloat in colour.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

A miniature world built from **flat-shaded low-poly geometry**: hexagonal columns whose height encodes the material (sand lowest, then grass terraces, grey rock), box houses with gable roofs, two-cone pines, faceted round trees, a few landmarks (a bevelled rock peak, a striped lighthouse, a windmill, a pier). The lens is **orthographic** at about 35° elevation: no perspective and no horizon. Distance dissolves into a **screen-space sky gradient**, so the island looks like a model suspended in colour. Every piece arrives on its own beat with a springy curve, and the story is told by what gets built.

Not a voxel game (no cubes of cubes, no pixel texture), not a tilt-shift photo (no perspective, no photo detail), not a smooth cartoon (no rounded shading, no outlines), not an infographic (one island, no charts floating over it). This example is a 2D rebuild: every face is a flat SVG polygon projected once; the camera only moves layers.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **World unit** R = a tile's circumradius (100 world px). Flat-top hexagons on an axial grid: `x = 1.5·R·q`, `z = √3·R·(r + q/2)`. Draw each column at 0.95 R so a thin gap separates tiles: the gaps show the darker sides behind and read as ambient-occlusion seams (never stroke the edges).
- **Projection** (orthographic, 35°): `screenX = x`, `screenY = z·0.574 − y·0.819`. Top faces squash to 0.574 of their depth (a hex top reads half as tall as it is wide); heights scale by 0.819.
- **Heights**: sand 0.42 R, grass ring 0.95 R, central plateau 1.65 R, grey rock tiles 0.58-0.75 R, the rock peak 0.95 R plus a bevelled octagonal cap (0.08 R bevel, 0.09 R cap). Grass tiles: a 0.15 R green band over brown dirt sides; sand tiles: a 0.08 R wet strip at the waterline; rock tiles: a 0.12 R light band over darker grey.
- **Flat shading from one sun** (right, above, slightly behind: shadows fall to the front left). Each face gets one of eight shade steps (8 % lighter, base, then 9 % steps toward the shadow tone); back faces are culled. A quarter of tile tops are jittered one step lighter or darker so the ground is not a spreadsheet.
- **Props are primitive assemblies**: pine = trunk + two hexagonal cones (0.3 R and 0.22 R radius, about 1.4 R tall); round tree = trunk + icosahedron (20 faces, 0.35 R across); palm = a leaning trunk and six thin fronds; house = 1-3 floors of 0.55 R boxes (0.8 × 0.6 R, rotated about 45° so two walls show), a 0.4 R gable roof with 15 % overhang, dark windows two per long wall, a door, sometimes a chimney.
- **Cast shadows**: the convex hull of the footprint and the footprint pushed away from the sun (0.5 × height left, 0.25 × height forward), the shadow tone at 20 %.
- **Water**: a flat saturated teal (the haze lightens it toward the horizon) with a few soft light rays slanting through the foreground, drifting a little. **Shallows**: one soft radial blob per tile (2.65 R radius, aqua) plus a smaller foam blob (1.3 R, near white); overlapping, they make one glowing shore.
- **Sky without a horizon**: a screen-space layer above the world: `--latar-2` at the top, opaque `--latar` by 26 % of the height, 72 % at 31 %, 26 % at 39 %, clear by 48 %. Whatever is far up the frame (the back of the island) fades into haze. A second screen-space gradient *under* the island darkens the deep water toward the bottom of the frame.
- **No outlines, no black.** Shadows and the gaps between tiles are the only darks. No textures, grain or blur.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar` is the haze band and the sky behind the titles; `--latar-2` is the sky at the top. A dark brand turns the sky to night and the world to dusk; a white brand gives a milky day.
- `--utama` is the built world's signal colour: the most common roof, the buoy and lighthouse stripes, the windmill cap, the boat's stripe, the price and contact pills, the top of the small tile icon. `--aksen` is the second roof colour. More roofs are mixed from them: `utama + aksen` (purple), `utama + orange`, `aksen + green`. One wall colour is a pastel pink mixed from `--utama`; the other walls stay pastel (cream, off-white, blue-grey).
- Nature keeps its own hues but follows the brand's light: sea teal, sand, grass, dirt, rock grey, pine green, leaf green and wood are fixed colours mixed 10-12 % with `--latar`.
- Fixed in every brand: window navy (#1f2a4a), the shadow tone (#173341), a near-white for highlights and foam, and the warm lamp yellow (#ffd27a), the only emissive colour.
- Text: titles in `--teks` with the key word in `--utama-di-latar`; the line under them in `--teks-redup` with the step label in `--aksen-di-latar`; pills are `--utama` with `--teks-di-utama`.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul`: a geometric heavy face in capitals with wide tracking: Poppins 800 at 92 px, letter-spacing 0.05 em, one line centred in the sky band (top at 88 px of 1080). Archivo Black or Inter 800 also suit.
- `--font-isi`: a rounded face for the line under the title: Fredoka 500 at 46 px (top at 226 px), preceded by a 60 px flat-shaded tile icon whose top is `--utama`; pills at 48 px with 38 px side padding. Poppins 500 also suits.
- **Titles behave like tiles**: each letter rises from under a thin water line (the title is clipped at its baseline), 0.035 s apart, with the pop spring (about 25 % overshoot), and sinks back below the line (0.25 s, 0.012 s apart) when the beat changes.
- All text lives in the top 280 px. At most seven words on screen. A wider brand font: shorten the words, do not go below 80 px.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Rise**: a tile is clipped at the front outline of its base at the height of whatever stands still in front of it (the water, or the sand and grass already built) and starts with its top at that line; it rises with `1 − e^(−6p)·cos(9p)` over 0.6 s (about 10 % overshoot), 0.045 s after the previous one. The foam ring (a hex outline 1.02 R at the emergence line; only its front half for a tile rising from open water) scales 1 → 1.45 and fades over 0.65 s; 3-10 droplets fly on parabolas (0.5-0.8 s, 50-140 px up, out 30-80 px).
- **Pop** (trees, landmarks): scale 0 → 1 from the base with `1 − e^(−4.5p)·cos(10p)` over 0.5-0.55 s (about 25 % overshoot).
- **Drop and stack** (houses, floors, pier planks): fall 240 px in 0.24 s `power2.in`, stretched 0.9 × 1.14; land squashed 1.16 × 0.8 and settle with the pop spring over 0.45 s. A new floor: the roof springs up one floor (`back.out(2.2)`, 0.28 s) and the floor drops in under it.
- **One piece per slot, accelerate by density**: tiles sweep 0.035 s apart; trees at 1/4 s, then 1/8, then 1/16 s; houses at 3/8, 1/4, then 1/8 s. Never two pieces landing on the same slot.
- **Counting**: a counter ticks once per landed piece and pumps 1.18 → 1 in 0.25 s.
- **Life**: windmill 90°/s; buoy and boat bob on the same wave (4 px, 1.8 rad/s, ±5° and ±2.5° tilt); three smoke puffs per chimney rise 170 px and fade over 2.2 s cycles; the light rays drift 14 px; the lighthouse beam sweeps by stretching between 15 % and 100 % of its length with |cos(1.6 t)|.
- **Holds**: each shot keeps one scale and drifts sideways (30-150 px, linear or cubic in-out); the last shot holds about 3 s with only life moving.

## 6. Camera grammar

The camera is a focus point in world px plus a scale; layers are drawn once and moved. Shots are joined by hard cuts on the beat, the scale changes only on a cut or in the one zoom out, and the projection never changes.

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tight close-up on one arrival (2.1×) | the bounce and the splash of a key piece | the hook, a milestone, a gag |
| Locked 3/4 wide (0.82×), slow sideways drift | the whole shape, the world on its own | a bare start, a fact, waiting |
| Medium (1.1×) while pieces pop | the shape growing | steps of a process |
| Medium-close (2.1×), 150 px truck over 3.5 s | details being added, counted | numbers, features of a product |
| Lateral truck along the front row (680 px in 2.5 s, cubic in-out) | a list, a sequence, a route | steps, a timeline, a delivery |
| Pure orthographic zoom out (1.05 → 0.79× in 0.9 s) | scale without perspective, the finished world | the payoff, the call to action |
| Hard cut on the beat | the next chapter | every beat change |

No dissolves, no perspective, no whip pans, no rotation of the view.

## 7. Native moves

- **Rise, one tile per beat.** In a close-up, tiles rise one per beat up through the island already built (or out of the open sea at the shore), each with a foam ring and spray, the hero piece last. *Fits content like:* a village emerging for a tourism page; a startup's first year; the first lesson of a new class; the opening of a short story about an island.
- **Growth by pops.** Trees pop with a 25 % overshoot, faster and faster, around the hero. *Fits content like:* two thousand trees planted by residents; a creator's followers growing; modules of a course unlocking; a garden through one spring.
- **Drop and stack, counted.** Houses fall, squash and settle while a counter ticks once per landing; later a roof springs up and a floor drops in. *Fits content like:* fourteen homestays built; orders shipped this week; finished chapters of a thesis; floors of a new office.
- **Lights on.** A landmark pops and its lamp glows with a sweeping beam exactly when the price appears. *Fits content like:* a package price; a network going live; opening night of an event; the lighthouse in a bedtime story.
- **Truck along the shore.** The camera slides along the front row while new pieces land: rock tiles rise, pier planks drop, a boat sails in. *Fits content like:* the steps of a booking; a delivery route; a timeline of a club; a journey across a map.
- **The world afloat.** A pure zoom out to the finished island floating in colour, smoke and the boat moving, name and contact rising from the water line and held. *Fits content like:* a call to book; a creator's channel world; a school campus; the last page of a story.

## 8. Pitfalls

- **Performance (live preview).** Draw every polygon once with baked coordinates and move only layers: the shallows, the still island, an *active* layer, small life layers. A piece that animates lives in the active layer only for its beat window and is moved into the still island on the next hard cut (that cut repaints the layers sharp at the new scale anyway); a pop inside a big SVG would repaint and re-layer the whole island every frame. Keep the scale fixed within a shot (scale drift re-rasters every frame); continuous motion (sails, boat, buoy, smoke, beam) is CSS transforms and opacity on small composited layers, updated only once visible, never SVG attribute changes per frame. No strokes on the tiles (they doubled raster time).
- **Pivot once.** Set each piece's `svgOrigin` before any scale is applied; changing it while a scale is active shifts the piece for good.
- **Rising through the surface.** Clip a rising piece at the front outline of its base extended upwards, at the height of the still tiles in front of it, and start it with its top at that line; a top sunk lower would show through the clip. Leave its lower sides (water to clip line) in the still layer so the seams in front stay dark.
- **Painter's order.** Sort by the depth of each base, tiles before the props standing on them; keep a prop within about 0.45 R of its tile centre or a neighbouring tile will cut it.
- **The haze band.** It hides the back of the island and carries the titles: frame the action in the lower 70 % and drop the first pieces of each beat where the camera looks.
- **Light brands.** A pale main colour on pastel walls loses the roof line: keep roof faces shaded (the slope away from the sun is two steps darker) and walls pastel, not white. Text colours come from the tokens and stay readable.
- **No live 3D, no real perspective, no blur, no outlines.** Fake depth with the projection, shade steps, haze and parallax-free orthographic moves.

## Variation space

The world (island, orchard, factory floor, campus, planet), what grows, the opening and the ending are free. Structures: **erosion** (a finished world loses pieces one by one until the essential one remains), **two worlds** side by side trading pieces until they join, **a year in four seasons** on one fixed island with the palette carrying the story. Openings: mid-construction, the finished world first then a push to one tile. Endings: a close-up on the last piece landing, the world packed away (pieces fly up and stack), daylight flooding a night island.

## Measured from the reference

A 12-second film: close-up 1 s, wide 1 s, medium growth about 2.5 s, medium-close building about 3.5 s, wide hold about 3 s. In wides the island fills 0.45-0.5 of the frame width; a hex top reads half as tall as wide; terrace steps are about 0.8 R. Samples: sky top #b2d4e5, haze #c4d9de, sea #218b9b darkening to #208797 at the bottom, shallows #68c2b6, grass #86ba58, dirt #7e5330, sand #e7d29d, rock #b0b2b1.

# Low-poly island: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.25, medium 2.5, long 3.5.

## hook

- en: close-up: tiles rise one per beat with a foam ring and spray, the hero piece last; the title's letters rise from a water line
- id: close-up: ubin naik satu per ketukan dengan cincin buih dan percikan, bagian utama terakhir; huruf judul naik dari garis air

## problem

- en: a piece sinks back under the water with a splash and leaves a gap; the camera holds wide on the empty spot
- id: satu bagian tenggelam lagi dengan percikan dan meninggalkan celah; kamera diam lebar di tempat kosong itu

## fact

- en: locked 3/4 wide of the island with a slow drift; one piece lands with a bounce as the line and tile icon appear
- id: pulau dilihat lebar dan tenang; satu bagian mendarat memantul saat kalimat dan ikon ubin muncul

## step

- en: one piece pops per beat (trees, then houses), faster and faster; the line names the step number
- id: satu benda tumbuh tiap ketukan (pohon, lalu rumah), makin cepat; kalimatnya menyebut nomor langkah

## compare

- en: two islands side by side, one bare and one built; pieces hop across the gap one by one
- id: dua pulau berdampingan, satu gundul satu jadi; benda melompat ke seberang satu per satu

## number

- en: houses drop, squash and settle one by one; the counter ticks once per landing and pumps
- id: rumah jatuh, gepeng lalu memantul satu per satu; angka naik satu tiap rumah mendarat

## proof

- en: tight close-up on one finished piece while life moves around it: smoke, a turning mill, a bobbing boat
- id: close-up satu bangunan jadi sementara dunia hidup: asap mengepul, kincir berputar, perahu bergoyang

## offer

- en: the camera trucks along the shore; a lighthouse pops and lights up, its beam sweeping, as the price pill pops
- id: kamera menyusuri pantai; mercusuar muncul dan menyala, sinarnya menyapu, tepat saat harga muncul

## cta

- en: pure zoom out to the finished island floating in colour; name and contact rise from the water line, held 3 s
- id: zoom mundur ke pulau jadi yang mengapung di warna; nama dan kontak naik dari garis air, diam 3 detik

## payoff

- en: the last piece lands in a close-up, then a cut to the whole island alive, held 2 s
- id: bagian terakhir mendarat dalam close-up, lalu potong ke seluruh pulau yang hidup, diam 2 detik

      const END = 15, R = 100, K = 0.574, C = 0.819; // R = jari-jari ubin; ortografis, elevasi 35°
